Meal Master case study

UX/UI Case Study &
App Design

About the App

Meal Master is a meal planning app that customizes its meals to your personal health and dietary needs. You can set your content to be provided as per your health situation. The app can partner with groceries to deliver healthy items online directly from the app.

The Process

  • Research
  • User Persona
  • Ideate
  • Design
  • Prototype
  • Test

User Research

Case Study

95.5 %Want to improve their health and food habits
70.2 %Spend a long time searching for recipes and planning their meals
50.1 %Have trouble finding healthy recipes suited for their health

The Problem

  • People are having difficulties with maintaining a healthy eating lifestyle
  • User spends a long time planning their meals and shopping for groceries
  • User finds it difficult to find suitable recipes for themselves. Everybody is different and unique.

The Solution

  • A user-guided meal planner which provides recipes containing ingredients that are beneficial for each particular user.
  • An available interface that allows you to create, and order your shopping list.

User Persona

Meet Lisa

Lisa, 32, is a full time Digital Marketer, and a mother of two. She lives in Ramat Gan.

Lisa suffers from an iron deficiency and has low blood pressure, she does not know which foods would be beneficial to her health.

Her long hours and tight schedule make it challenging to find and cook a variety of recipes that are healthy.

Frustrations

  • Often spends long hours searching for recipes, shopping for groceries.
  • Suffers from health issues that are unique to her.

Goals

  • Live a healthier lifestyle and feel better overall
  • Enjoy a variety of healthy, delicious recipes in a convenient and easy manner

Lisa Brown, 32

  • Female
  • Mother of 2
  • Ramat Gan, Israel
  • Digital Marketing
  • Iron deficient, low blood sugar
  • Cooks for her family

Online Workout Program case study

UX/UI & Brand Design

Online Workout Program

Project Overview

About The Project

This case study focuses on the Website and Logo Design for Esther Taub's Lifestyle Program. The Lifestyle Program is a popular online workout program for women. The program promotes a positive and healthy approach to fitness and focuses on the physical and mental aspects of well-being. The website and logo design are essential for effectively conveying the program's values and engaging potential users.

Problem Statement

  • Users would struggle to navigate through the website. It was not intuitive nor engaging which was leading to a suboptimal user experience.
  • Branding was inconsistent, leading to decreased recognition and trust among its target audience.
  • Logo was outdated and did not properly reflect the brand's values.

Our Role

  • Research
  • User Flow
  • Style Guide
  • UX/UI Design

Main Goals

Description

The design aims to create a cohesive brand identity for the Lifestyle Program. The website design aims to provide a user-friendly and intuitive experience for visitors, ensuring they can easily access workout videos and other program resources. The logo design seeks to capture the essence of the Lifestyle Program, incorporating elements that represent its values of health, happiness, and body positivity.

Research

Target Audience

Primarily women seeking to improve their physical and mental well-being. They are individuals who desire a positive and inclusive approach to fitness, with a focus on body positivity and celebrating their bodies. They are likely to have busy schedules and value convenience, seeking workout solutions that can be easily integrated into their daily lives.

Jewish Inspiration App

A daily Torah companion for people who want to do what matters to them, every day.

  • RoleUX/UI design
  • PlatformMobile app
  • FocusDaily habit
The problem

Finding a large block of time to connect spiritual and practical Torah learning is difficult. When the day gets busy, what matters most is the first thing to slip.

The solution

HAYOM is a little, fun way to make sure you do what's important to you every day. One short Torah teaching a day, in Hebrew and English, and a single tap to say you were mindful of it.

How it works

  1. Read today's teaching. A short quote with its source, in Hebrew and English side by side.
  2. Tap "I was mindful of this today". One tap, a little "Shkoyach!", and your day is counted.
  3. Watch your journey grow. A seven-day timeline checks off each day you complete.

The flow

The prototype takes a new user from the splash screen to their first daily quote in a few taps.

Design details

  • Bilingual by default. Each quote shows the English and the Hebrew side by side, with the key phrase in bold.
  • Photography that matches the quote. The sunset opens the app and a lion illustrates the courage quote, fading into the page below.
  • A restrained palette. Deep indigo for actions and text, a soft cream-yellow gradient for backgrounds, and a bright yellow reserved for the mindfulness button.
  • Serif type for the teachings. The wordmark and quotes use a serif, and the interface uses a clean sans-serif.
  • Simple navigation. Four tabs (Today, My Journey, Profile and Favorites) in a floating bar at the bottom.
  • Settings. Notifications, dark mode, languages and the privacy policy are one tap away from the profile.
